clue.text: Ungenerous when tipsy

explanation.definitionFit: Both a miser and someone a little drunk are described in everyday slang by the same short word.

clue.text: Aviation ace has smug group holding up trial

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, propping it up

parts.note: a trial is a test
PI, short for pious, means sanctimonious or smug
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A flying hero brings a self-satisfied team along to help with an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'holding up' puts PILOT under TEST. PI (short for pious) is a crossword convention for smug.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace aviator may be the one who flies new aircraft to check their performance before service.

clue.text: Fish-eaters are fools

definitions.meaning: people easily tricked; to gull is to dupe

explanation.definitionFit: The seabird and the dupe share a word; a gullible person is one easily fooled.

clue.text: Lace-makers in rags

definitions.meaning: people who tat, making lace by hand with a shuttle

explanation.definitionFit: To tat is to make tatting lace, so its practitioners share a word with shredded remnants of clothing.

clue.text: Ripley set out to become a writer

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Ripley and set are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone called Ripley sets out on a career in authorship.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, author of An Inspector Calls.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist and dramatist is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Flexible individual in a factory

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for a factory

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: A bendable worker on the factory floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliant material bends easily; it is supple.

clue.text: Visionary keeps record of suggestions

indicators.note: a record of suggestions is a list of ideas, so the suggestions come first

parts.note: suggestions are ideas put forward
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A dreamer keeps a written log of proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is only a link: the visionary keeps, or is, an idea list.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist is a dreamer with lofty visions of how things should be.

clue.text: Still need to serve Len's ice-cream

indicators.note: to cream is to beat ingredients together, so the letters of Len's ice are mixed

explanation.surface: Len needs his ice-cream served, and quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' is not food but the verb, beating the letters of LEN'S ICE into a new order. 'Still' is the noun, as in the still of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The still of the night is its quiet hush, a total absence of sound.

clue.text: It's the most foolish, anyway

definitions.meaning: read as two words, having the smallest amount of wisdom

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means having the smallest share of wisdom; whole, it is an old adverb meaning at any rate.

clue.text: Long tale about the Orient

indicators.note: the word for a tale goes about, around, the compass letter

parts.note: a yarn is a long story
the Orient is the East, E on a compass

explanation.surface: A lengthy story set in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave it.

clue.text: Game — rosalie gets upset eating it

indicators.note: eating means the rearranged name takes the small word inside it
upset signals that the letters of rosalie are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rosalie throws a tantrum over a card game, then gobbles something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the name into SOLAIRE; 'eating' puts the two-letter word inside. 'Game' is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a one-player card or peg game, also called patience.

clue.text: A climber from brasilia naturally gifted

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A naturally gifted mountaineer from Brazil's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of brasiLIA NAturally. 'climber' is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that scrambles up trees.

clue.text: Notice small number on the back door

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up in public
N is the short form of number, 'small' signalling the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sign with a little number stuck on the rear entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear gate or side entrance, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Heavyweight with enduring style

parts.note: long-lasting, so long
ton is fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer with lasting flair.
explanation.walkthrough: A long ton is the British imperial ton of 2,240 pounds, heavier than the American short ton.
explanation.definitionFit: This imperial measure of 2,240 pounds is a literal heavy weight.

clue.text: Six-footer army boss beset by libido

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the letters for the boss sit inside the word for libido

parts.note: libido is sexual desire, lust
OC is Officer Commanding, a military commander

explanation.surface: A tall army commander tormented by sexual desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The swarming grasshopper is an insect, and every insect walks on six legs.

clue.text: Always left during game if pessimistic

indicators.note: during puts the letters for always and left inside the game

parts.note: chess is a board game
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone who always feels abandoned mid-game is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy, joyless outlook is a downbeat, hopeless one.

clue.text: Notable Anglicans involved in espionage

indicators.note: involved in places the church letters inside the word for spying

parts.note: espial is an old word for spying or observation
EC is the Established Church, the Church of England

explanation.surface: Distinguished churchmen caught up in spying.
explanation.walkthrough: EC stands for Established Church, England's state church, to which Anglicans belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means particular, exceptional, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Scottish port imbibed by head churchman

indicators.note: imbibed by means drunk in, so the port is taken inside the word for head

parts.note: a head is a leader or chief
Ayr is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A senior cleric drinks Scotch port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the wine, but it is the harbour town AYR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a non-ordained person licensed to lead parts of church services.

clue.text: The wren — a fantastic bird

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful or fantasised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praising the wren as a marvellous little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterhen, or moorhen, is a dark marsh bird of the rail family.

clue.text: The hype about a player

indicators.note: the word for hype goes about, around, the single letter

parts.note: spin is promotional hype or slanted presentation

explanation.surface: The publicity surrounding a star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, a player on the stage.

clue.text: Pedestrian isn't content when coated with oil

indicators.note: content means the slangy contraction is what the abbreviation contains

parts.note: PED is a short form of pedestrian, as on a crossing sign
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A walker grumbles at being smeared in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the adjective meaning happy, but it is the noun: what the pedestrian holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture done in oils has been applied with oil colours on canvas.

clue.text: Exclude eastern diocese? That's only just!

parts.note: to bar is to shut out or exclude
Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, eastern England, gives its name to a diocese

explanation.surface: Shutting out an East Anglian bishopric is a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means scarcely, by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: American houses a minor of wayward nature

indicators.note: houses means the short form of American holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a means one, which is I in Roman numerals
less means minor, as in St James the Less, also called James the Minor

explanation.surface: A US citizen gives shelter to a wild youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a minor' looks like a child, but 'a' gives I and 'minor' gives LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means drifting without purpose or direction.

clue.text: Reluctant Irish support for the old bible

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, the King James translation of 1611
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Irish backing for the King James translation is half-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'support for' puts ERSE under AV.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means being opposed to or unwilling to do something.

clue.text: Master sounds beastly and obsequious

indicators.note: sounds means the word for master is said out loud and written as it is heard

parts.note: sir is the respectful address to a master
vile means nasty or beastly

explanation.surface: A tyrannical master seems horrible, and his servants grovel.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the whole phrase SIR VILE is said aloud; the sound of SIR is written SER, and VILE stays as spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile behaviour is fawning and slavish, overly eager to please.

clue.text: Prophet without time to give guidance

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the prophet surrounds the letter for time

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who foresees the future

explanation.surface: A soothsayer with no time to offer counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tempts as 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer someone is to direct or guide them.

clue.text: See a member rage against extortioner

parts.note: V is short for Latin vide, meaning see, used in references
MP is Member of Parliament
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Watch a politician vent fury at a blackmailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire, figuratively, is someone who preys on others by draining them of money.

clue.text: Send out the children

definitions.meaning: distribute or release, as of stamps or a statement

explanation.definitionFit: One word means to distribute officially, and also offspring, as in dying without heirs.

clue.text: Standing up before going to court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Rising to one's feet before heading to the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, vertical.

clue.text: Attached to one's horse

parts.note: looks like devotion to a favourite animal, but describes being hitched up to it with straps

explanation.definitionFit: A horse in tack is yoked or strapped to a cart or plough, so whatever it pulls is fastened to it.

clue.text: I screened off the house

indicators.note: off suggests something gone off or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has fenced off their home.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, a home.

clue.text: Promise to get Sunday clothes

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: Vowing to dress in one's Sunday best.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or give one's solemn word.
